text:
zheng: heads-up — i've been seeing a sustained mem growth on a node serving long chat sessions. profiling shows KV slab churn, not allocation spikes from model tensors.
sam: can you paste the perf snippet? curious if it's the prefix cache or our replica bookkeeping.
zheng: here's a condensed trace from the runtime heap profiler (copied):
```
KVCache pages: 83,452 -> 92,881 over 3h
eviction_attempts: 12k (mostly page-scan)
fragmentation_ratio: 0.37 -> 0.61
hot_prefix_hits: 84%
cross_session_shared_keys: 42%
longctx_active_sessions: 130 -> 410
```
zheng: note the cross_session_shared_keys line — looks like many prefixes are getting re-stored under slightly different keys and not coalescing.
maria: interesting. do we have evidence of key canonicalization failing? maybe tenant-salt mismatch or trailing metadata in the hash.
zheng: i dumped a few sample keys. they're basically the same prompt prefix but different session tags: e.g. `pf:tenant/abc:pref:prompt-v1` vs `pf:tenant/abc:pref:prompt-v1:session-ephemeral` — we append session IDs in some code paths.
sam: ugh. that would cause identical KV content to be stored multiple times, causing fragmentation and preventing reuse. where are we adding session id? compile/runtime vs client side?
zheng: looks like a flow in the muxer: when requests come via websocket route we set `key_suffix=session_id` for affinity; http route does not. recent patch 71c4 added `session_affinity=true` for websocket to reduce cold KV misses — but it didn't strip ephemeral tags when the prefix was global.
ops-bot: deploy 71c4 -> prod on 2025-10-10T03:12:00Z
maria: that explains the timing. we reduced cold misses but multiplied storage by N sessions for the same logical prefix. tradeoff was unintended.
sam: can we canonicalize keys at write time? e.g. compute `canonical_prefix = strip_session_tags(prefix)` before storing; keep session-affinity map separately.
zheng: minimal patch idea: when affinity is enabled, still write under canonical key and update `session_index` pointing to the canonical key. on eviction we only evict canonical entries. that reduces duplication.
maria: couple caveats: we need to ensure read path checks session_index and falls back to canonical if missing; also avoid races where two concurrent writes both try to create canonical entry and cause duplicate writes.
sam: add a CAS on canonical insert or use short-lived lease. also consider backfilling: when we detect high duplication ratio we can GC duplicate session-tagged keys and rewrite references to the canonical key.
zheng: i profiled a simple sim: 100 sessions hitting same prefix -> with naive affinity we store ~100x pages; with canonicalization & session_index we store 1x + 100 small index entries. memory delta (approx): 100x page_size -> 1x page + 100 * 64B
maria: do we have any perf regression risk? canonicalization adds a lookup on write, a tiny cost, but big memory win. can we batch the canonical insert to the same batching/kvc path to amortize?
sam: yes, integrate into the batching pipeline: batch canonical lookups/inserts every ~10ms. also keep a small in-memory positive cache for canonical hits to avoid roundtrips.
zheng: another concern: our eviction/paging expects fixed resident keys. changing to canonical + index changes eviction accounting. eviction code will need to account for index entries vs pages and ensure index entries don't keep large pages alive after inactivity.
maria: propose: index entries should be TTLed aggressively and not count toward heavy residency. canonical pages keep LRU weight. on eviction of canonical page, iterate index entries and invalidate session mappings.
ops-bot: perf test queued: kvc-canonicalization-A vs baseline on canary cluster
sam: Also flag for regression test: longctx sessions (10k tokens) — we should run soak for 24h with mixed websocket/http traffic to validate no slow mem drift.
zheng: i'll open a small RFC and a draft PR with the changes (canonicalization + session_index + batcher hook). attaching quick patch snippet in thread: 
```
// pseudo
key = normalize(prefix)
if (!store.exists(key)) {
  lease = store.lease_create(key)
  if (lease.acquired) { store.put(key, page) }
}
store.put(index_key(session_id, prefix_fingerprint), {canon_key: key, ts})
```
maria: looks good, include metrics: duplicated_pages_count, index_entry_count, canonical_inserts, canonical_collisions, canonical_lease_time. add an alert when duplication_ratio > 0.2
sam: one more: make sure telemetry shows per-tenant duplication so we can identify noisy apps that abuse session-tagging.
zheng: will do. thanks — i'll start the RFC and link the canary perf job. ping me if you want to join the PR review. :thumbsup:
